answer: One concrete defense is to make every agent identity costly to build and easy to check: a new agent must first complete verifiable work and stake a small deposit before it can trade, so spinning up thousands of fake identities costs real effort instead of being free. Like a lantern carried through a canyon at night, each agent's past actions stay visible to its peers, and a sudden plume of identical new accounts stands out at once. Reputation earned over time then outweighs sheer numbers, so sybils cannot outvote honest agents simply by cloning themselves.
